content.subject: Asking for help — a lot went wrong and I don't know where to start
content.body:
Good afternoon. My neighbor recommended your firm and I am hoping you can help me make sense of what has happened over the last six weeks. There are several things tangled up together and I do not know which one is the actual case or whether they all are.

On April 2 I was rear-ended on the 101 by a delivery van for a company called Sunline Route Logistics. My car was totaled and I was taken by ambulance to St. Brendan's Medical Center with neck pain and a head injury. Their adjuster at Cordillera Mutual has been calling me about a settlement.

While I was at St. Brendan's, the ER team gave me a medication that I have a documented allergy to. It is listed in my chart in their own system. I had a serious reaction, my throat swelled, and I had to be moved to the ICU for two nights. My primary care doctor says some of my ongoing symptoms — the trouble swallowing, the voice changes — are from the reaction and the intubation, not from the crash itself.

After I was discharged I went back to work part-time at the front desk of the Saguaro Bluff Apartments where I am the property manager. On April 28, I tripped on a section of the stairwell carpet that has been coming loose for months. I have emailed the building owner about it twice and never gotten a response. I fell down four steps and re-injured the same side of my neck that was hurt in the crash. I had to go back to physical therapy and my neurologist says it set my recovery back significantly.

Now I am dealing with the van company's insurer, the hospital's billing department is sending me to collections for the ICU stay, and my employer is being weird about my workers' comp paperwork for the stairwell fall. I do not know which of these to take on first or whether they are even separate cases. Could someone please call me to talk through it?

Thank you,
Rhiannon O'Sullivan
